title: r says /r/
parentNote: Today is /r/, and it is the one sound so far where nothing touches anything: the tongue pulls back and bunches up in the middle of the mouth, the tip hovers without landing, and the lips round a little. Because the lips round, /r/ and yesterday's /w/ come out almost the same for a lot of children — "rat" turns into "wat", "rig" into "wig" — and the fix is the tongue, not the lips: ask them to feel the back of the tongue lift and pull back while the tip stays down. The other slip is "ruh", which makes "rip" into "ruh-ip"; stretch it instead, rrrrrip, because /r/ is a sound you can hold. Say the pair rig and wig for them a few times and let them tell you which is which before they read anything.

activities.mouthCue: Pull your tongue back and bunch it up in the middle. The tip points at the roof but never touches it.
activities.prompt: You can hold this one for as long as your breath lasts. Try it: rrrrrr.
Your lips round for both. Only one of them moves your tongue.
Three hums. One has the tongue tip up on the ridge, one has it pulled back, one has no tongue at all.
Stretch the first sound, then snap the last one shut.
Nearly rat. This time the end hums instead of stopping.
Small vowel in the middle. Do not let an uh sneak in after the /r/.
Say it next to wag. Your tongue is the only thing that changes.
Two sounds at the front, squashed together. A pop at the back, then the long /r/.
The rim is the edge that goes all the way round a cup.
This is the hard pair. Tongue back for one, lips only for the other.
Does the tongue touch behind your teeth, or does it stay back?
All three start alike. Hold on to the very last sound.
